rules: Glob `ruststream_sqs_sns::prelude::*` in a routes file and `ruststream::prelude::*` in a handler file; a body that names a per-message FIFO setting globs this crate's prelude (page: Components > Broker > Prelude).

Describe a subscription with `SqsQueue::new(queue)` and its `wait`, `visibility` and `create_if_missing` steps, or with a bare queue name for the defaults (page: Components > Subscriptions > SqsQueue).

Chain the queue steps after the framework's at the mount site, `b.include(handler.batch(nonzero!(10)).wait(..))`, through the `SqsSubscription` trait in the prelude (page: Components > Subscriptions > SqsSubscription).
Take a batch as a `&[T]` parameter and size it with `.batch(n)`: one `ReceiveMessage` call is one batch of at most ten messages (page: Components > Subscriptions > Batches).
Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(queue)` right after `include`, always both halves, which become the queue's redrive policy (page: Components > Settlement > Dead letters).

Return `HandlerOutcome::retry_after(delay)` for a later retry: SQS hides the same message for the delay, within 12 hours of its receive, and it keeps its receive count (page: Components > Settlement > retry_after).

Enable the `sns` feature and bind a reply with `.out_reply(SnsPublish::default())` to fan it out from a topic; the broker's default `SqsPublish` sends a reply to a queue (page: Components > SNS > SnsPublish).

Set one FIFO message's group and deduplication id with the `group_id` and `deduplication_id` steps of `SqsPublishSteps`, or a position's group with `Publish::default().group_id(..)` (page: Components > Publishing > group_id).

Bound a slot whose body names those steps as `Out<impl Publisher<Options = SqsPublishOptions>, Marker>`, and any other slot as `Out<impl Publisher, Marker>` (page: Components > Publishing > SqsPublishOptions).
Take credentials from the AWS SDK's default chain with `SqsBroker::new()`, or pass a prebuilt `SdkConfig`, timeouts included, to `SqsBroker::from_config` (page: Components > Broker > Credentials).
Test the production app with the `testing` feature: `ruststream::testing::TestApp::start` connects `SqsBroker` in process, addressed as `tb.broker::<SqsBroker>()` (page: Components > Testing).
Run the same test body against LocalStack or AWS with `TestApp::start_live` for the queues, timeouts and credentials the service finds there (page: Components > Testing > Live).
